12209               	; 	' ======================================================================
12210               	; 	' THE SCANNER
12211               	; 	' ======================================================================
12212               	; 	' Rows 21-23, 16 chars wide, centred: 48 characters whose PATTERNS are
12213               	; 	' poked directly, so a moving dot costs two writes and no name-table
12214               	; 	' traffic. With the flip (DESIGN.md 2a) this is how you know where Harry
12215               	; 	' is at all -- he can be one pixel off-screen and completely invisible.
12216               	; 	'
12217               	; 	' Rows 21-23 all sit in the THIRD screen third, so every scanner pattern
12218               	; 	' is at base 4096 and no third-selection arithmetic is needed.
12219               	; 	'
12220               	; 	' BOTH DOTS ARE WHITE and Kelly's BLINKS. The manual wants Kelly black
12221               	; 	' and Harry white, but this is the TMS9918's two-colours-per-8x1-cell
12222               	; 	' mode: a black dot and a white dot on the same pixel row of the same
12223               	; 	' character cannot both exist. Blinking distinguishes them with one
12224               	; 	' colour, which is what RallyX does with its player dot.
12225               	; 	' THE STEPS MOVE, AND EVERY ESCALATOR ON SCREEN MOVES WITH THEM. A flight
12226               	; 	' is twelve characters -- six per direction, sliced out of a rendered
12227               	; 	' 64x40 bitmap by genart.py -- so rewriting those twelve PATTERNS animates
12228               	; 	' the lot: 96 bytes, no name-table traffic, and the same cost whether one
12229               	; 	' flight is visible or ten. The phases slide the cells ALONG the slope, so
12230               	; 	' the steps travel up the flight rather than drifting sideways.

12256               	; 	' ONE PHASE PER PASS, AND NEVER MORE. There are four phases covering an
12257               	; 	' 8 px period, so advancing by the frame delta ALIASES: at fdv 2 the
12258               	; 	' pattern flips between two positions half a period apart and the
12259               	; 	' direction stops being readable, and at fdv 3 the sequence runs 0,3,2,1
12260               	; 	' -- the staircase visibly runs BACKWARDS, carrying its steps down while
12261               	; 	' the rider goes up. That is the wagon-wheel effect, and no amount of
12262               	; 	' phase arithmetic fixes it: a 4-phase cycle can only be stepped by 1.
12263               	; 	'
12264               	; 	' So the ANIMATION is the clock here, and the rider is paced from it --
12265               	; 	' see move_kelly, which advances him by the same fixed 2-and-1 per pass
12266               	; 	' rather than by fdv. Locking the two together is the only way they
12267               	; 	' cannot drift, and it is what "the player moves at the rate the steps
12268               	; 	' carry him" actually means. The cost is that a ride takes 36 passes
12269               	; 	' rather than 36 frames, so it slows down when the loop does -- which is
12270               	; 	' the honest behaviour for a machine that is carrying you.

12284               	; 	#if NES
12285               	; 	' A VBLANK OF ITS OWN, AND THIS IS THE WHOLE-SCREEN FLASH.
12286               	; 	'
12287               	; 	' PPUBUF is not flushed when it is written -- it ACCUMULATES for the whole
12288               	; 	' pass and the NMI empties it in one go, so every VPOKE the radar makes,
12289               	; 	' every HUD digit and this upload all land in the SAME vblank. And the
12290               	; 	' handler's copy loop does not stop when vblank ends: it runs to the end of
12291               	; 	' the descriptor and then writes PPUADDR and both PPUSCROLLs, which
12292               	; 	' mid-frame re-points the PPU's own render address. The rest of that frame
12293               	; 	' is drawn from the wrong place. On screen that is not a dropped tile, it
12294               	; 	' is the ENTIRE PICTURE jumping for a frame -- which is what has been
12295               	; 	' reported, repeatedly, as the screen flashing on an escalator.
12296               	; 	'
12297               	; 	' The arithmetic says it cannot be anything else. NTSC vblank is about
12298               	; 	' 2273 CPU cycles; NMI entry, the flicker test and OAM DMA spend ~560 of
12299               	; 	' them before a single byte is copied. A copy descriptor costs ~50 cycles
12300               	; 	' plus 14 a byte, so these six characters -- 96 bytes, because a tile is
12301               	; 	' SIXTEEN bytes in two bitplanes, not eight -- are ~1400 on their own.
12302               	; 	' That leaves about 270 cycles, or SIX single-byte pokes, for everything
12303               	; 	' else the pass queued. The radar alone beats that whenever a dot moves.
12304               	; 	'
12305               	; 	' Nothing smaller fixes it, because the overrun is per FRAME, not per
12306               	; 	' second: slowing the animation down just makes the bad frames rarer.
12307               	; 	' Splitting the six characters across two frames tears the staircase, and
12308               	; 	' only three of the six have a constant second bitplane, so dropping a
12309               	; 	' plane does not buy a frame's worth either. What DOES work is giving the
12310               	; 	' upload a vblank with nothing else in it: this WAIT flushes the pass's
12311               	; 	' radar and HUD writes, and the descriptor queued below is then almost all
12312               	; 	' the next vblank has to carry -- ~1960 cycles of 2273, inside the window
12313               	; 	' with room to spare.
12314               	; 	'
12315               	; 	' IT COSTS ONE FRAME A PASS, on the two screens that carry a flight and
12316               	; 	' nowhere else -- esc_tick has already returned on the other six. The
12317               	; 	' rider is paced from the animation rather than from the frame delta (see
12318               	; 	' below), so a slower pass slows the ride too and the two cannot drift.
12319               	; 	WAIT
12320               	; 	#endif
12321               	; 	' ONLY THE CELLS THAT MOVE, AND ONLY THIS SCREEN'S. genart.py measures
12322               	; 	' which cells move -- the step cells and the COMPOSITE copies of them
12323               	; 	' that cross a floor -- and groups them WEST then EAST, because only one
12324               	; 	' direction is ever on screen: screen 0 carries a west flight and screen
12325               	; 	' 7 an east one.
12326               	; 	'
12327               	; 	' THIS IS THE ONLY PER-PASS WORK UNIQUE TO THESE TWO SCREENS, and it is
12328               	; 	' `define_char`, which in bitmap mode is LDIRVM3 -- the TRIPLE copy, once
12329               	; 	' per screen third. It therefore costs three times what the character
12330               	; 	' count suggests, which is why these screens run slower than the rest.
12331               	; 	'
12332               	; 	' THE WEST SCREEN USED TO COST HALF AS MUCH AGAIN, because it carries TWO
12333               	; 	' flights: floor 1's crosses into a shop floor and floor 3's into the

12670               	; 	' ------------------------------------------------- the scanner's furniture
12671               	; 	' Without this the scanner is two dots in a void: you can see THAT Harry is
12672               	; 	' somewhere, but not what he is near, which is the one thing you actually
12673               	; 	' need when he is off-screen. Floor lines say which level, the slashes say
12674               	; 	' where that floor's escalator is, and the bar says where the elevator is --
12675               	; 	' exactly the three things the manual lists.
12676               	; 	'
12677               	; 	' FURNITURE AND DOTS ARE SEGREGATED BY PIXEL ROW ON PURPOSE, and a level
12678               	; 	' band is now FOUR rows, one per colour, because a pixel row carries
12679               	; 	' exactly one colour here:
12680               	; 	'
12681               	; 	'   +0  GREY    escalator head, and the elevator car
12682               	; 	'   +1  GREY    the air of that floor
12683               	; 	'   +2  GREY
12684               	; 	'   +3  YELLOW  the floor line -- and NOTHING else goes here
12685               	; 	'
12686               	; 	' THE FIRST THREE ROWS ARE THE FLOOR'S AIR AND EVERYTHING LIVES IN THEM:
12687               	; 	' the escalator's three-step diagonal, the lift car, and both actors, all
12688               	; 	' three pixels tall. They are grey in the table, and the Kop and the
12689               	; 	' crook recolour their own CHARACTER as they move (scan_mark) -- which is
12690               	; 	' what lets both of them fill the band instead of getting a pixel row
12691               	; 	' each. Eight pixels of this canvas is half a screen of the store, so
12692               	; 	' they are almost never in one character; when they are, they merge.
12693               	; 	'
12694               	; 	' Shrinking from six rows bought eight empty pixel rows, four above the
12695               	; 	' instrument and four below, so it no longer butts against the shop floor
12696               	; 	' above it or the bottom of the screen.

12969               	; 	' A LEVEL BAND IS SIX PIXEL ROWS ON THE NES AND FOUR ON THE TI.
12970               	; 	'
12971               	; 	' It was six everywhere once. It shrank to four to buy eight empty pixel
12972               	; 	' rows -- four above the instrument and four below -- so the scanner did
12973               	; 	' not butt against the shop floor above it and the bottom of the screen.

12976               	; 	' thirty rows to the TI's twenty-four, so the strip runs past the canvas to
12977               	; 	' the bottom edge and the grey either side of the instrument is real cells
12978               	; 	' rather than blank rows inside it. That gives the band its two rows back,

13142               	;
13143               	; 	' Blank the canvas by WRITING zeros rather than copying 384 of them out
13144               	; 	' of ROM. This runs twice a game -- at setup and on a new Krook -- so a
13145               	; 	' loop costs nothing anybody can perceive, and it hands the fixed area
13146               	; 	' back the best part of half a kilobyte, which is the budget that
13147               	; 	' actually binds. Paced in bursts: a few hundred VDP writes in a single
13148               	; 	' frame are silently dropped (CLAUDE.md 3A).
13149               	; scan_wipe:
13150               cvb_SCAN_WIPE
13151               	; 	' THIS ADDRESS IS A CHARACTER CODE IN DISGUISE, AND IT WENT STALE.
13152               	; 	' 4096 is the pattern table's BOTTOM THIRD -- rows 16-23, which is
13153               	; 	' band 0 and the radar together -- and the canvas characters begin at
13154               	; 	' genart's SCAN_FIRST, so the base is 4096 + SCAN_FIRST*8. It was
13155               	; 	' written out by hand as 4096 + 160*8 when SCAN_FIRST was 160; art

13813               	; #if NES
13814               	; 	' ----------------------------------------------------------------------
13815               	; 	' Attributes select a palette per 16x16 quadrant. gennescolor.py derives
13816               	; 	' eight screen tables; draw_screen stages one in nesb, masks fixtures,
13817               	; 	' then uploads all 64 bytes through nes_attrs_put within one vblank.
13818               	; 	' A MESSAGE BOX GOES GOLD ON DARK BLUE, and the caller says which four
13819               	; 	' bytes in #nav.
13820               	; 	'
13821               	; 	' The text's paper is index 1 and its ink index 3 (see the font upload);
13822               	; 	' over the store those are P0's green and gold -- the same green the box is
13823               	; 	' sitting on, which is what made the messages hard to read. P1 is the HUD's
13824               	; 	' palette, dark blue and gold, so pointing the box's attribute bytes at it
13825               	; 	' gives a message the same treatment as the score line.
13826               	; 	'
13827               	; 	' FOUR BYTES AND NOT ONE MORE. An attribute byte covers four characters by
13828               	; 	' four, and the box is sized and placed to cover exactly four of them
13829               	; 	' (gentitle.py BOX_ROW/BOX_COL/BOX_W): byte columns 2..5, which is name
13830               	; 	' columns 8..23. Anything wider would recolour shop floor beside the box.
13831               	; 	'
13832               	; 	' THIS IS A ROUTINE BECAUSE IT WAS WRITTEN OUT TWICE AND MISSED A THIRD
13833               	; 	' TIME. GOT HIM! kept the store's colours while the other boxes changed,
13834               	; 	' and nothing failed -- it is a readable message in the wrong palette.
13835               	; 	' checkmsg.py now fails the build if a message box is drawn without one of
13836               	; 	' these beside it.
13837               	; 	'
13838               	; 	' Nothing puts them back, because nothing needs to: every path out of a
13839               	; 	' message box redraws the screen, and draw_screen calls nes_attr, which
13840               	; 	' rewrites all sixty-four.

13963               	; 	' more like it -- four compares, four assignments and four jumps to walk a

14272               	; 	' every radar poke and HUD digit the pass had made. The copy then ran past

14275               	; 	' read as intermittent corruption.

14353               	;
14354               	; 	' THE BONUS IS COUNTED OUT, NOT AWARDED. Dropping the whole sum into the
14355               	; 	' score in one frame tells the player a number; ticking the clock down a
14356               	; 	' unit at a time, with the score climbing and a beat under each step,
14357               	; 	' tells them what the number was FOR. It is the pay-off for every second
14358               	; 	' they saved, and every arcade game of this era spends a moment on it.
14359               	; 	'
14360               	; 	' It also costs nothing to get right: the loop already has to run down
14361               	; 	' `tsec`, so the animation IS the calculation, and the repeated-addition
14362               	; 	' note below stops applying -- each step adds one band's worth.
14363               	; 	'
14364               	; 	' x100 for Krooks 1-9, x200 for 10-15, x300 from 16. Two independent
14365               	; 	' sources agree on those bands; the manual's own wording suggests
14366               	; 	' 1-8 / 9-16 / 17+ and DESIGN.md 0 records the disagreement.
14367               	; 	'
14368               	; 	' IN UNITS OF TEN, WHICH IS WHAT THE SCORE IS COUNTED IN, so the bands are
14369               	; 	' 10 / 20 / 30 and not 100 / 200 / 300.
14370               	; 	'
14371               	; 	' They were 100 / 200 / 300 and paid TEN TIMES the right bonus -- 1,000 a
14372               	; 	' time unit where the original pays 100. `add_score` takes `#addv` in units
14373               	; 	' of ten (the prize beside it is `#addv = 5` for fifty points, and the bonus
14374               	; 	' Kop threshold is `#nextk = 1000` for ten thousand), so writing the band in
14375               	; 	' POINTS here shifted every tally one decimal place. Reported from play as
14376               	; 	' "it seems like you awarded 1000 per time unit left" -- exactly right.
14377               	; 	'
14378               	; 	' Nothing failed: 1,000 a unit is a plausible-looking number, the digits
14379               	; 	' all line up, and the only symptom is a score that runs away. The tell is
14380               	; 	' a constant written in a different unit from the routine it is passed to,
14381               	; 	' which is the same class of fault as the px-per-pass speeds in 3A.
14382               	; 	'
14383               	; 	' (This is also why the old comment here said "#bval MUST BE 16-BIT: 300
14384               	; 	' does not fit in a byte". At 10 / 20 / 30 it would, but it stays 16-bit
14385               	; 	' because `#addv` is, and a byte here would buy two bytes of ROM in
14386               	; 	' exchange for a truncation trap the next time somebody edits a band.)
14387               	; bonus_count:
14388               cvb_BONUS_COUNT

14530               	;
14531               	; 	' AND IT ENDS ON ITS LAST BLIP -- there is no closing accent.
14532               	; 	'
14533               	; 	' Two were tried. The bench's own ending for this variant rose a fourth,
14534               	; 	' to 2,542 Hz, and a square wave there is a shriek -- the same fault the
14535               	; 	' pickup was rewritten for. Dropping it an OCTAVE BELOW the ticks, to
14536               	; 	' 518 Hz, was reported the same way, and that one cannot be too high by
14537               	; 	' any measure: it is the lowest note in the effect.
14538               	; 	'
14539               	; 	' So the complaint is not the pitch, it is the extra note. A tally is
14540               	; 	' arithmetic, and arithmetic finishes when the last term is added; a
14541               	; 	' flourish after it is a second event the player has to interpret, and
14542               	; 	' the HUD has already said the clock is empty. The count stops when the
14543               	; 	' counting stops.
14544               	;
14545               	; 	' `calc_bonus` USED TO LIVE HERE and computed the whole sum by repeated
14546               	; 	' addition, to dodge two hazards at once: `tsec * bmul` is an 8-bit
14547               	; 	' product (a 50-unit capture in the x300 band pays 15,000, six times past
14548               	; 	' a byte), and multiplying properly lands on the MPY/r0 hazard where a
14549               	; 	' 16-bit variable read straight after being multiplied returns the
14550               	; 	' product's high word. Counting the bonus out a unit at a time (above)
14551               	; 	' removes the multiply entirely rather than working around it -- the loop
14552               	; 	' the player watches IS the arithmetic.
14553               	; 	'
14554               	; 	' It also fixed the last-tick case for free: `bn_loop` tests `tsec = 0`
14555               	; 	' on entry, where the old `FOR bi = 1 TO tsec` would have run its body
14556               	; 	' once and paid a full multiplier for no time at all (CLAUDE.md 3A).
14557               	;

14601               	; 	' THE CAST IS NOT TAKEN AWAY YET -- hide_all now runs AFTER the beat.
14602               	; 	'
14603               	; 	' It used to run here, so the moment the clock emptied, Harry and the
14604               	; 	' thing that had just hit him vanished and the sound played over an empty
14605               	; 	' store. The hit that ENDS a round is the worst case: `do_hit` sets tout
14606               	; 	' before the freeze starts and the main loop leaves on the very next pass,
14607               	; 	' so the hit sound gets one tick and everything is already gone.
14608               	; 	'
14609               	; 	' The pause drains the sound; leaving the actors up means it drains over
14610               	; 	' the picture that caused it. Nothing is moving -- the pause ticks sfx_tick
14611               	; 	' and nothing else -- so it is a held tableau, not a frozen game.
14612               	; 	' THE MESSAGE BOX, ON THE GAME SCREEN AND NOT INSTEAD OF IT.
14613               	; 	'
14614               	; 	' It used to CLS before GAME OVER, so the last thing the player saw was
14615               	; 	' the store being deleted and then two words on an empty field -- which
14616               	; 	' reads as the program ending rather than as the game ending. The store
14617               	; 	' stays; the message sits in the middle of it.
14618               	; 	'
14619               	; 	' THE BOX IS THE FONT'S OWN BACKGROUND. Every font character is black on
14620               	; 	' HUD_BG (dark blue), so a row of SPACES is a solid dark blue bar. A blank
14621               	; 	' row above and below the text is a frame for the price of two strings and
14622               	; 	' no new characters, and it reads against the store because nothing else on
14623               	; 	' the playfield is that colour.
14624               	; 	'
14625               	; 	' THIRTEEN WIDE, WHICH IS THE LONGEST MESSAGE PLUS ONE EITHER SIDE.
14626               	; 	' HE GOT AWAY and THE BIPLANE are both eleven. Every string below is padded
14627               	; 	' to exactly thirteen so the box has straight edges, and column 10 puts it
14628               	; 	' at columns 10-22 -- centre 16, the screen's.
14629               	; 	'
14630               	; 	' THE REASON IS ALWAYS ON THE SAME ROW, and that is what lets one layout
14631               	; 	' serve both cases. Losing a life draws three rows around it; losing the
14632               	; 	' last one draws two more ON TOP, so GAME OVER appears above the reason
14633               	; 	' rather than replacing it. Printing the reason at a different row for each
14634               	; 	' case would need `PRINT AT` with a variable, and every other PRINT in this
14635               	; 	' program uses a constant.
14636               	; 	#if NES
14637               	; 	' FLUSH THE PASS BEFORE DRAWING A BOX. PPUBUF accumulates for a whole loop
14638               	; 	' pass and is emptied by one NMI, so a message box -- sixty-four cells,
14639               	; 	' sixty-four single-byte descriptors -- was landing in the same vblank as
14640               	; 	' every radar poke and HUD digit the pass had made. The copy then ran past
14641               	; 	' the end of vblank and the tail was DISCARDED at the PPU: a box with
14642               	; 	' characters missing, and the cut moving from run to run, which is why it
14643               	; 	' read as intermittent corruption.
14644               	; 	'
14645               	; 	' One WAIT here empties the buffer; the box's own writes then self-pace,
14646               	; 	' because WRTVRM waits when PPUBUF fills. That is also why the TITLE never
14647               	; 	' needed this and must not have it: it is drawn at boot with nothing else
14648               	; 	' queued, and a WAIT per run made its twelve runs appear one frame at a
14649               	; 	' time -- a logo that visibly assembled itself.
14650               	; 	WAIT
14651               	; 	#endif

14910               	;
14911               	; 	' A SOUND STILL PLAYING WHEN THE ROUND ENDS IS ALLOWED TO FINISH.
14912               	; 	'
14913               	; 	' This used to open with a bare `GOSUB snd_off`, which cut it dead. That
14914               	; 	' was not an accident: the decay counters are ticked by the MAIN LOOP, and
14915               	; 	' this pause REPLACES the main loop, so a tone left latched with nothing
14916               	; 	' ticking it hangs for the full ninety frames -- the sticky-audio failure
14917               	; 	' this game has already shipped twice. The answer is to DRAIN the counters
14918               	; 	' rather than to stop silencing.
14919               	; 	'
14920               	; 	' CLEAR THE PENDING LATCHES FIRST. sf* flags are sounds that have not
14921               	; 	' happened yet; left set, the drain below would START one and the pause
14922               	; 	' would end with a fresh note ringing into the next round.
14923               	; 	'
14924               	; 	' THEN TICK sfx_tick WHOLE, not some decay-only part of it. The five
14925               	; 	' counters do not all live in one place: sot, sht and spt are a block at
14926               	; 	' the tail, but spz (the prize arpeggio) and swt (the jump warble) tick up
14927               	; 	' among the code that starts sounds. Draining only the tail would finish a
14928               	; 	' footstep and still cut the arpeggio, which is the one effect with a
14929               	; 	' phrase worth saving. Calling the whole routine also leaves the write
14930               	; 	' order on CHANNEL 2 alone, which spz and spt share.
14931               	; 	'
14932               	; 	' EVERY THIRD FRAME, because the main loop runs about 2.5 frames per pass
14933               	; 	' and this loop waits one frame per turn. Ticking every frame would play
14934               	; 	' everything at two and a half times its tuned speed. Three frames a tick
14935               	; 	' is ~17% slow and gives 30 ticks against the longest effect's 20 passes.
14936               	; 	'
14937               	; 	' THE LOOP COUNTS TICKS, NOT FRAMES, which is what makes the pacing free.
14938               	; 	' Counting 91 frames and firing on every third needs a second counter, an
14939               	; 	' increment and a test -- 48 bytes, on a fixed area with 66 left. Counting
14940               	; 	' 31 TICKS of three WAITs each is the same 93 frames and the same three
14941               	; 	' frames per tick, with none of that. The duration changes by two frames.
14942               	; 	'
14943               	; 	' snd_off still runs at the END, as the backstop for anything the drain
14944               	; 	' did not finish.
14945               	; pause_beat:

15382               	;
15383               	; 	' THE LOW-TIME WARNING IS SILENT. There was a beep a second under ten, and
15384               	; 	' it was the wrong instrument for the job: the last ten seconds are the
15385               	; 	' busiest part of a round, so a repeating tone arrives exactly when the
15386               	; 	' player most needs to hear the hazards, and it fought the prize arpeggio
15387               	; 	' for channel 2 as well. The flash says the same thing and says it in the
15388               	; 	' place the player is already looking.
15389               	;
15390               	; 	' FOOTSTEPS ARE NOISE, AND ON THE NOISE CHANNEL -- testsounds variant A.
15391               	; 	'
15392               	; 	' They were two alternating TONES on channel 0, which is neither what the
15393               	; 	' original does nor a good use of a channel: the recording says a footstep
15394               	; 	' is a short burst of white noise, and channel 3 was sitting unused while
15395               	; 	' the footsteps and the jump sweep shared channel 0 and had to take turns.
15396               	; 	'
15397               	; 	' TESTSOUNDS RUN D: a SHORT tick at the measured RATE.
15398               	; 	'
15399               	; 	' The two dials are independent and both were tried at the bench. The
15400               	; 	' 2600 plays a 64 ms burst every 165 ms -- six a second -- and variant A
15401               	; 	' copies both. Ten a second was tried on the way here and reads as
15402               	; 	' hurrying rather than running. What D changes is not the cadence but the
15403               	; 	' TICK: two frames rather than four, and a notch louder to carry at half
15404               	; 	' the length. Same six a second, less of it.
15405               	; 	'
15406               	; 	' EIGHT A SECOND, AND THE ACCUMULATOR NOW CARRIES ITS REMAINDER.
15407               	; 	'
15408               	; 	' sfw counted pixels and the trigger did `sfw = 0`, THROWING AWAY whatever
15409               	; 	' was past the threshold. kspd is about four pixels a pass, so a threshold
15410               	; 	' of 17 did not fire at 17 -- it fired at the first multiple past it, about
15411               	; 	' 20, and every rate this was ever set to came out slower than the number
15412               	; 	' said: the "six a second" was 5.2 and the "ten" that read as hurrying was
15413               	; 	' really 8.7. Subtracting the threshold instead keeps the fraction, so the
15414               	; 	' rate is what it claims to be at any walking speed.
15415               	; 	'
15416               	; 	' MEASURED OFF THE COLECOVISION: 14 px, about 7.4 a second.
15417               	; 	'
15418               	; 	' It was 15 px and 6.9 a second, picked between an 8.0 that read as
15419               	; 	' slightly hurried and a 6.1 that read as trudging -- a judgement between
15420               	; 	' two other judgements, with nothing underneath it. The ColecoVision
15421               	; 	' recording settles it: footfalls land every 0.130 s across a twelve-second
15422               	; 	' continuous run, which is 7.7 a second, and that is the one finding in the
15423               	; 	' whole sound analysis the method resolves EXACTLY -- a rhythm rather than a
15424               	; 	' pitch, counted off the RMS track rather than inferred from a spectrum.
15425               	; 	' (colecosounds variant 1A; assets/sfx/sfxref-coleco.md has the working.)
15426               	; 	'
15427               	; 	' 104 px/s over 14 px is 7.43 a second. 13 px would give 8.00, and 7.7 sits
15428               	; 	' almost exactly between them -- so this is the nearer of the two, and it is
15429               	; 	' also the one that does not walk back into the 8.0 that was rejected by ear.
15430               	; 	'
15431               	; 	' WHY THE GAME KEEPS A DISTANCE AND THE BENCH KEEPS A CADENCE. The bench
15432               	; 	' plays a fixed eight frames between steps because it has no walking to tie
15433               	; 	' them to; the game accumulates PIXELS TRAVELLED, so the feet keep time with
15434               	; 	' the legs when he is slowed or stopped. Matching "7.4 a second" therefore
15435               	; 	' means matching it AT HIS WALKING SPEED, and assumes the ColecoVision's
15436               	; 	' crook walks at ours -- which the recording cannot confirm.
15437               	; 	'
15438               	; 	' The dial is this one constant and the subtraction below, which must stay
15439               	; 	' threshold + 1 or the carry is wrong.
15440               	; 	'
15441               	; 	' SOT = 2 IS THE SHORTEST TICK THERE IS, and 1 is SILENCE. The decay block
15442               	; 	' below runs LATER IN THE SAME sfx_tick, so a count of 1 is decremented to
15443               	; 	' zero on the pass that set it and the note-off fires before the sound has
15444               	; 	' lasted any time at all. 2 survives to the next pass, which is one pass of
15445               	; 	' sound -- about 42 ms against the bench's 33, as close as a per-pass timer
15446               	; 	' gets, and the reason the bench and the game cannot sound identical.
15447               	; 	'
15448               	; 	' Register 4 is white noise at the fastest rate.
15449               	; 	'
15450               	; 	' VOLUME 9, WHICH IS UNDER EVERYTHING ELSE ON PURPOSE. The hit, the prize
15451               	; 	' and the jump are 12 and 13, and they happen ONCE; footsteps play for the
15452               	; 	' whole round. At 13 they were level with the events they are supposed to
15453               	; 	' sit beneath, so the effects that carry information had nothing to stand
15454               	; 	' out from. The tone version was 7 for the same reason -- noise does read
15455               	; 	' quieter than a tone at the same number, which is why this is 9 and not
15456               	; 	' back to 7.
15457               	; 	IF sfw > 13 THEN

15786               	; 	' keeping one readable thing in bank 0 means a bank-selection mistake shows
15787               	; 	' as "text survives, art does not" rather than a uniformly blank screen,
15788               	; 	' which is a genuinely useful thing to have when a bank goes wrong.
15789               	; 	'
15790               	; 	' THE FONT HAS A BANK OF ITS OWN, and the reason is not its size.
15791               	; 	'
15792               	; 	' Bank 1 was FULL -- six spare bytes of 8,192 -- which shut the door on
15793               	; 	' moving anything else out of the fixed area, and the fixed area is the
15794               	; 	' only budget that cannot be grown (linkticart writes exactly three
15795               	; 	' loader pages and discards the rest; they are the 32K expansion's RAM at
15796               	; 	' >A000, not cart ROM). A second bank costs a bigger cart -- five pages
15797               	; 	' round up to eight, so 32 KB becomes 64 KB -- and buys back the ability
15798               	; 	' to keep evacuating data out of code.
15799               	; 	'
15800               	; 	' THE FONT IS THE RIGHT TENANT because it is read ONCE. Two DEFINEs copy
15801               	; 	' it into VRAM at setup and nothing looks at it again, so it is the only
15802               	; 	' block here that can sit on a page which is not permanently mapped. See
15803               	; 	' setup_font: bank 2 is selected for those two statements and bank 1 for
15804               	; 	' the whole of the rest of the program.
15805               	; 	'
15806               	; 	' EVERYTHING ELSE STAYS IN BANK 1, because everything else is read during
15807               	; 	' play -- art on a screen crossing, templates on a band blit, the lookup
15808               	; 	' tables every pass. One permanently-mapped bank for all of it means
15809               	; 	' there is no switch to miss.
15810               	; 	#if TI994A
15811               	; 	BANK 2
15812      0774     BANK_0_FREE:	EQU >fffe-$
     **** ****     > .rept

15847               	; 	' ONE PROMPT AT A TIME, NOTHING ELSE ON THE SCREEN, AND NO NUMBERS UNTIL
15848               	; 	' THEY ARE TYPED. There is no heading and no instructions: a page showing
15849               	; 	' exactly one question does not need to explain that one digit answers it,
15850               	; 	' and the second question does not exist until the first is answered.
15851               	; 	'
15852               	; 	' Showing the CURRENT values first was the obvious thing and it cost more
15853               	; 	' than it gave -- two draw routines, a "fire keeps what is shown" escape to
15854               	; 	' make the display mean something, and the defaults had to be applied here
15855               	; 	' as well as in new_game so the page had numbers to show at all. None of it
15856               	; 	' survives: every digit on screen is one the player just typed. Four
15857               	; 	' strings became two, a two-field loop became a straight line, and the page
15858               	; 	' got SMALLER while getting quieter.

16771               	; 	' CHASE (game_tune, genmusic.py) plays during a round on PLAY SIMPLE NO
16772               	; 	' DRUMS: TWO voices on channels 0 and 1 only. The TI effects split by
16773               	; 	' channel -- 0 the jump warble (swt), 1 hits and the escape (sht), 2
16774               	; 	' prizes/lives/tally, noise the footsteps -- so only jumps and hits
16775               	; 	' collide, and those DUCK the music: PLAY NONE freezes the player where
16776               	; 	' it is (it only clears music_mode; the song position is untouched), and
16777               	; 	' PLAY SIMPLE NO DRUMS resumes from the same note once they end.
16778               	; 	'
16779               	; 	' The test runs BEFORE sfx_tick writes anything, and counts the pending
16780               	; 	' latches (sfj/sfh/sfe) as well as the running counters, so the player
16781               	; 	' has let go of the channel before the effect's first write -- otherwise
16782               	; 	' the next vblank would stomp that first frame.
16783               	; 	'
16784               	; 	' Called from the main loop only, never from pause_beat: the round-end
16785               	; 	' pause is effects-only (pause_beat stops the music on entry).
16786               	; 	'
16787               	; 	' IT LIVES IN BANK 2 and the main loop maps bank 2 around the call: the
16788               	; 	' fixed area's UNOPTIMISED first pass had 156 bytes left and this body
16789               	; 	' did not fit. A bonus: PLAY game_tune runs with bank 2 already mapped,
16790               	; 	' which is the page the player records for the tune. Nothing here may
16791               	; 	' BANK SELECT (it would unmap itself).

16993               	; 	' ---------------------------------------------------------------- TITLE, IN BANK 2
16994               	; 	' title_draw, title_input, title_wait and title_setup run only while the
16995               	; 	' title is up, so on the TI they live in bank 2 and boot selects bank 2
16996               	; 	' around them -- moved with setup_font and init_tables to make room for the
16997               	; 	' music player (see MOVED TO BANK 2 below). Inside them there is NO
16998               	; 	' BANK SELECT: code here that selected bank 1 would unmap itself. Their
16999               	; 	' one bank-1 read, the marquee lamp art, goes through title_bulb in the
17000               	; 	' fixed area, which maps bank 1 for the DEFINE and bank 2 back before
17001               	; 	' returning here. run_list stays fixed: the round-end message boxes use it

17092               	; 	'   * CLAUDE.md claimed every other game here dodged the problem by not
17093               	; 	'     reading up/down. EIGHT of them do read it -- Adventire, Astiroids,
17094               	; 	'     HardHatMack, Ms. Pac-Man, RallyX, Structris, UFO, Bust-A-Bobble --
17095               	; 	'     and not one has a calibration or has ever shown the fault.
17096               	; 	'   * It never fired on the machine this is developed on: the notice it
17097               	; 	'     prints when it detects a stuck axis has never appeared.
17098               	; 	'   * The original evidence was that the game "came up and would not
17099               	; 	'     start" -- and the first version BLOCKED until the axis cleared. That
17100               	; 	'     symptom is indistinguishable from the several input bugs since found
17101               	; 	'     and fixed for real: keys arriving at a screen that was not listening
17102               	; 	'     yet. The diagnosis was probably one of those.
17103               	; 	'
17104               	; 	' It also cost two bugs of its own: forty frames of a drawn but deaf title

17108               	; 	' If a stuck axis ever does appear it will be obvious -- the player will

17164 692C A684     	data wait
17165               	; 	' THE MARQUEE CHASES WHILE THE TITLE WAITS.
17166               	; 	'
17167               	; 	' ONLY TWO CHARACTERS CHANGE PER STEP. At any moment exactly one of the
17168               	; 	' four lamps is blank; a step lights the one that was blank and blanks the
17169               	; 	' next one round. Redefining all four would be twice the work for the same
17170               	; 	' picture.
17171               	; 	'
17172               	; 	' IT IS BELOW THE INPUT READS, deliberately. This loop's history is input
17173               	; 	' bugs -- a screen that was drawn but not listening, a keypress eaten by a
17174               	; 	' stability filter -- so nothing that is merely decoration goes in front of
17175               	; 	' the polling. A dropped frame of animation is invisible; a dropped
17176               	; 	' keypress is what took three sessions to find.
17177               	; 	' `bphs` IS WHICH LAMP IS DARK, and a step is: light that one, move on,
17178               	; 	' darken the next. The character number is arithmetic rather than a
17179               	; 	' four-way branch -- DEFINE CHAR takes an expression, so the whole chase
17180               	; 	' is two calls and no `IF` ladder. The ladder version was eight DEFINE
17181               	; 	' CHARs across four branches and cost about three hundred bytes for the
17182               	; 	' same picture.
17183               	; 	'
17184               	; 	' TWO CALLS, NOT FIVE. Lighting all four and then darkening one is the
17185               	; 	' same result and reads more simply, but two separate DEFINEs can have a
17186               	; 	' vblank between them, so the sign would show ALL lamps lit for a frame
17187               	; 	' every step -- a flash rather than a chase. Only ever changing the two
17188               	; 	' lamps that actually change cannot do that.
17189               	; 	bfr = bfr - 1
17190 692E D020  34 	movb @cvb_BFR,r0
     6930 2086

17257               	; 		' A SECOND STAGING AREA, AND THIS IS THE WHOLE MARQUEE BUG.
17258               	; 		'
17259               	; 		' nes_escd does NOT copy anything. It builds the tile into the RAM
17260               	; 		' buffer `#nesb` and hands the NMI a five-byte descriptor holding a
17261               	; 		' POINTER to it; the copy happens at the next vblank. Both marquee
17262               	; 		' writes happen in the same pass, so with one buffer the darken call
17263               	; 		' overwrote the staged LIT bytes before the NMI had read either --
17264               	; 		' and then BOTH descriptors copied bulb_off.

17267               	; 		' itself out: "it animates a little bit and goes out". Nothing fails,
17268               	; 		' because both writes are perfectly valid and land exactly where they
17269               	; 		' were addressed -- they just carry the same sixteen bytes.

17271               	; 		' The lit call staged at nesb(0); this one stages sixteen bytes up.
17272               	; 		' nesb is 96 bytes for the escalator's six characters and the
17273               	; 		' escalator never runs on the title screen, so the room is free. The
17274               	; 		' pointer is put back immediately: esc_tick stages at offset 0 and
17275               	; 		' would otherwise write its six characters one tile off.

17504               	;
17505               	; 	' 8-3-8 IS EDGE-TRIGGERED AND ANY STRAY DIGIT RESETS IT (see title_wait).
17506               	; 	'
17507               	; 	' It used to read cont1.key raw every pass and test only for the digit it
17508               	; 	' wanted next. That worked -- but only because 8-3-8 ALTERNATES, so holding
17509               	; 	' 8 cannot advance past the first step. It is an accident of the sequence
17510               	; 	' rather than a design, and it had two costs: 8,5,3,9,8 opened this page as
17511               	; 	' readily as 8,3,8, and a key that READS as held for many frames got a free
17512               	; 	' walk through the state machine.
17513               	; 	'
17514               	; 	' That second one is not hypothetical on this machine. ALPHA LOCK shorts a
17515               	; 	' keyboard line -- and Classic99 defaults to invertcaps, so it reads DOWN
17516               	; 	' with the host's Caps Lock UP -- and this page was reached twice from
17517               	; 	' single keypresses while testing an unrelated change.
17518               	; 	'
17519               	; 	' The reset is the DEFAULT rather than a test for a particular wrong digit:
17520               	; 	' Bust-A-Bobble resets only on a stray 3 and still lets 8,5,3,8 through.
17521               	; 	' ------------------------------------------------------- 838 setup page
17522               	; 	' ======================================================================
17523               	; 	' A NEW GAME / A NEW KROOK
17524               	; 	' ======================================================================
17525               	;
17526               	; 	' ---------------------------------------------------------------- MOVED TO BANK 2
17527               	; 	' setup_font and init_tables run ONCE, at power-on, and read nothing from
17528               	; 	' bank 1 -- so on the TI they live here, in bank 2, and the caller selects
17529               	; 	' bank 2 around the GOSUB. They moved to make room for the TI music player
17530               	; 	' (title music, ~1.2 KB of runtime in the fixed area): with it, the
17531               	; 	' UNOPTIMISED first assembly ran past >FFFF and xas99 rejected branches
17532               	; 	' before shortbranches.py could run (CLAUDE.md 3A, TI short-branch note).
17533               	; 	' A routine placed here must not BANK SELECT (it would unmap itself) and
17534               	; 	' must not read bank 1: init_tables' one bank-1 read, jarc_tbl, stayed
17535               	; 	' behind as init_jarc. On ColecoVision and NES this is ordinary code.
17536               	; setup_font:
17537               cvb_SETUP_FONT
17538               	; 	' Flicker stays OFF. CVBasic's is all-or-nothing -- it rotates all 32
17539               	; 	' slots, so Kelly would strobe too, and he is the one thing the player
17540               	; 	' must never lose. He is sprite 0 instead: the VDP drops the
17541               	; 	' HIGHEST-numbered sprites on an over-full scanline, so slot 0 is the
17542               	; 	' one slot that can never disappear.
17543               	; 	SPRITE FLICKER OFF
17544 6B00 0200  20 	li r0,>0400
     6B02 0400     
17545 6B04 F800  30 	socb r0,@mode
     6B06 834E

17547               	; 	#if NES
17548               	; 	' No BORDER on this machine: the area outside the picture is the backdrop,
17549               	; 	' palette entry 0, which title_draw and draw_screen already set.
17550               	; 	#else
17551               	; 	' DARK BLUE, NOT BLACK. The TMS border is the strip outside the 256x192
17552               	; 	' picture, and on a real set it is a good part of what the player sees --
17553               	; 	' left at the default black it made a hard frame around the shop. Dark blue
17554               	; 	' is the sky's own colour and the paper every piece of text sits on, so the
17555               	; 	' picture runs out to the edge of the tube instead of stopping at it.
17556               	; 	BORDER 4
17557 6B08 0200  20 	li r0,1024   ; 4*256
     6B0A 0400

     6B20 8C02     
17565 6B22 0300  22 	limi 2
     6B24 0002     
17566               	; 	#endif
17567               	;
17568               	; 	#if NES
17569               	; 	' THE NES'S TWO STRUCTURAL DIFFERENCES, SETTLED ONCE, HERE.
17570               	; 	'
17571               	; 	' 1. WHERE THE PATTERNS LIVE. In 8x16 sprite mode the sprite pattern table
17572               	; 	'    is chosen by bit 0 of each OAM tile byte and the PPUCTRL bit is
17573               	; 	'    ignored -- and every pattern number in this game is a multiple of
17574               	; 	'    four, so that bit is always 0 and the sprites are nailed to $0000.
17575               	; 	'    nes_bgbank therefore moves the BACKGROUND to $1000 rather than trying
17576               	; 	'    to move the sprites, which also lands the background patterns at
17577               	; 	'    address 4096, exactly where the TMS bitmap mode's third screen third
17578               	; 	'    had them -- so the radar's pattern writes need a stride and nothing
17579               	; 	'    else.
17580               	; 	'
17581               	; 	' 2. COLOUR DOES NOT MAP AND IS NOT PRETENDED TO. The NES colours in 16x16
17582               	; 	'    attribute blocks; this game colours per character, two colours a
17583               	; 	'    cell. So the store is drawn in ONE ink and the actors get four
17584               	; 	'    palettes, picked by the low two bits of the colour argument the
17585               	; 	'    SPRITE statements already pass -- 1 (black) -> dark grey, 4/8 (blue)
17586               	; 	'    -> blue, 14 (grey) -> grey, 11/15 (skin, white) -> white. Nothing in
17587               	; 	'    the game source has to know.
17588               	; 	ASM JSR nes_bgbank
17589               	; 	ASM JSR nes_apuon
17590               	;
17591               	; 	' Grey is shared index 0 during gameplay. Other indices are per region.
17592               	; 	' gennescolor.py assigns P3 only to counter quadrants, retaining green
17593               	; 	' wall and gold floor colours. Fixtures with black outlines use P0.
17594               	; 	PALETTE 1,26			' P0: green, black, gold
17595               	; 	PALETTE 2,15			' black escalators and fixture outlines
17596               	; 	PALETTE 3,40
17597               	; 	PALETTE 5,1			' P1 HUD/upper skyline: blue, pink, gold
17598               	; 	PALETTE 6,36
17599               	; 	PALETTE 7,40
17600               	; 	PALETTE 9,38			' P2 lower skyline: orange, black, gold
17601               	; 	PALETTE 10,1			' unused skyline index 2: navy message bottom border
17602               	; 	PALETTE 11,40
17603               	; 	PALETTE 13,26			' P3 counters: green, blue, gold
17604               	; 	PALETTE 14,1			' same navy in counter quadrants
17605               	; 	PALETTE 15,40
17606               	;
17607               	; 	' AND FOUR FOR THE ACTORS, which DO get one each because a sprite carries
17608               	; 	' its own palette number. nes_spal maps the TMS colour every SPRITE
17609               	; 	' statement already passes onto these four.
17610               	; 	PALETTE 17,18			' 0 -- blue   Kelly's trousers
17611               	; 	PALETTE 21,15			' 1 -- black  hats, Harry's stripes, the Kop's dot.
17612               	; 					' FIFTEEN, NOT ZERO: on this palette $0F is
17613               	; 					' black and $00 is a dark GREY, so every hat
17614               	; 					' and every stripe was coming out grey.
17615               	; 	PALETTE 22,23			' black sprite palette, index 2: brown suitcase outline
17616               	; 	PALETTE 25,39			' 2 -- skin   faces and the biplane
17617               	; 	PALETTE 26,16			' 2 colour 2 -- GREY, the lift car on the radar
17618               	; 	' AND THE BALL IS RED, which it already is on the TI: C_BALL is TMS 8,
17619               	; 	' medium red. nes_spal sends that to sprite palette 2, and palette 2's
17620               	; 	' colour ONE is the skin tone -- so on this machine the ball came out the
17621               	; 	' same pale orange as a face.
17622               	; 	'
17623               	; 	' A sprite here is ONE bitplane, so its pixels are whichever index the
17624               	; 	' upload writes and the OAM byte only chooses the palette. The lift car on
17625               	; 	' the radar already solved this: it is uploaded with `nink = 2` and reads
17626               	; 	' palette 2's second entry. The ball does the same with the THIRD, which
17627               	; 	' nothing else uses.
17628               	; 	PALETTE 27,22			' 2 colour 3 -- RED, the bouncing balls
17629               	; 	PALETTE 29,48			' 3 -- white  Harry, the carts, the lift car
17630               	;
17631               	; 	#endif
17632               	; 	#if TI994A
17633               	; 	#else
17634               	; 	nespw = 2			' NES/Coleco start on a 2-frame pass
17635               	; 	#endif
17636               	;
17637               	; 	' THE ONE AND ONLY BANK SWITCH THE PROGRAM EVER MAKES, and it happens
17638               	; 	' here, before the first frame.
17639               	; 	'
17640               	; 	' There are two data banks now. Bank 1 holds everything read while the
17641               	; 	' game is running -- sprite and store art, the templates, the lookup
17642               	; 	' tables -- and it is selected at the end of this routine and never
17643               	; 	' changed again, so every VARPTR/PEEK read in the program is reading a
17644               	; 	' page that is permanently mapped. That is the property that makes
17645               	; 	' banking safe here: a missed BANK SELECT returns bytes from the wrong
17646               	; 	' page with no error at build or run time, so the safest number of
17647               	; 	' switches during play is none.
17648               	; 	'
17649               	; 	' Bank 2 exists to hold data that is read ONCE, at setup, and never
17650               	; 	' again. The font is exactly that: two DEFINEs copy it into VRAM and
17651               	; 	' nothing reads font_bits or font_col for the rest of the run. So it can
17652               	; 	' live on a page that is mapped for the length of those two statements.
17653               	; 	'
17654               	; 	' IF THIS EVER FAILS IT FAILS LOUDLY. Select the wrong bank here and the
17655               	; 	' font is garbage on the title screen, immediately and unmistakably --
17656               	; 	' which is the same diagnostic the font used to provide by staying out of
17657               	; 	' the banks altogether, recovered for free.
17658               	;
17659               	; 	#if NES
17660               	; 	' THE FONT IS SENT WITH A COLOUR TABLE SO ITS PAPER IS NOT THE BACKDROP.
17661               	; 	'
17662               	; 	' With `#ncol = 0` the uploader puts ink `nink` on index 0 -- the UNIVERSAL
17663               	; 	' backdrop, black in the game -- so every character of text sat in its own
17664               	; 	' black box. The score line was a black strip across the top of a blue sky.
17665               	; 	'
17666               	; 	' Index 0 cannot be set per region (it is one colour for the whole screen),
17667               	; 	' so the only way to give text a ground is to put its PAPER on another
17668               	; 	' index, and paper is written into the second bitplane when the character
17669               	; 	' is uploaded. Hence a table: $B4 is light yellow on dark blue, which
17670               	; 	' nes_inkmap sends to index 3 and index 1.
17671               	; 	'
17672               	; 	' ONE FONT, NOT TWO. The first attempt at this made a SECOND copy of the
17673               	; 	' font at codes 197.. so the HUD could differ from the message boxes, and
17674               	; 	' that was both unnecessary and impossible: in game the HUD and the boxes
17675               	; 	' are the same text and want the same treatment, and 197..207 is only
17676               	; 	' ELEVEN free codes -- 208 up is the radar canvas (genart's SCAN_FIRST),
17677               	; 	' which scan_wipe rewrites as raw pattern memory every frame. The 59-char
17678               	; 	' copy appeared to upload and was scribbled over from its twelfth character
17679               	; 	' on. See checkpat.py, which now knows the canvas owns those codes.
17680               	; 	'
17681               	; 	' What index 1 IS comes from the attribute table, per region: the HUD row
17682               	; 	' is on P1 (dark blue, below) and the store is on P0.
17683               	; 	#nsrc = VARPTR font_bits(0)
17684               	; 	nchr = 32
17685               	; 	ncnt = 59
17686               	; 	ntab = 1
17687               	; 	#ncol = VARPTR nes_fcol(0)
17688               	; 	nink = 3
17689               	; 	GOSUB nes_def
17690               	; 	#else
17691               	; 	DEFINE CHAR 32,59,font_bits
17692 6B26 0204  20 	li r4,32
     6B28 0020     
17693 6B2A 0205  20 	li r5,15104
     6B2C 3B00     
17694 6B2E 0200  20 	li r0,cvb_FONT_BITS
     6B30 6CC6     
17695 6B32 06A0  32 	bl @jsr
     6B34 AE2A     
17696 6B36 A1FA     	data define_char
17697               	; 	#endif
17698               	; 	' Without this the font keeps whatever CVBasic left in the colour table --
17699               	; 	' white on transparent -- which over a green store made the HUD unreadable.
17700               	; 	'
17701               	; 	' THIS WAS A VPOKE LOOP AND IT WAS THE SLOWEST THING IN THE BOOT: 1,416
17702               	; 	' writes of one constant, paced by 24 WAITs, which is what made the title
17703               	; 	' fill in visibly instead of appearing. DEFINE COLOR does the same job in a
17704               	; 	' single call with interrupts off, and it writes all three screen thirds
17705               	; 	' itself -- define_color always takes the LDIRVM3 triple-copy path, which is
17706               	; 	' also why esc_deck_col and floor0_colour below CANNOT use it: they patch
17707               	; 	' one third each.
17708               	; 	'
17709               	; 	' The table is 472 identical bytes (genfont.py emits it beside the glyphs).
17710               	; 	' It reads as waste and is not: it lives in the data bank, which had 860
17711               	; 	' bytes spare, while the loop it replaced cost time in the one place the
17712               	; 	' player is made to wait.
17713               	; 	#if NES
17714               	; 	' no colour table on this machine -- see nes_setup
17715               	; 	#else

     6B3A 0020

     6B3E 3B00

     6B46 AE2A

17723               	;
17724               	; 	' AND THE TITLE'S DISPLAY FACE, WHICH IS HERE FOR THE SAME REASON THE
17725               	; 	' FONT IS. Forty characters -- ten letters, four cells each -- drawn at
17726               	; 	' 16x16 so the game's name reads as a name rather than as a line of body
17727               	; 	' text. It is 640 bytes of pattern and colour and bank 1 had 370 free, so
17728               	; 	' it could not go there; it did not need to, because it is read ONCE, by
17729               	; 	' these two statements, and never again.
17730               	; 	'
17731               	; 	' Loading it inside the bank-2 window the font already opens means the
17732               	; 	' program still makes exactly ONE bank switch in its life.
17733               	; 	' IN TWO PIECES, AND THE SPLIT IS NOT TIDINESS. The character table has
17734               	; 	' 0..31, 91..95 and 182..207 free -- sixty-three codes, but the longest
17735               	; 	' run is thirty-two and the face needs forty. Loading it as one block at
17736               	; 	' 182 ran it into the RADAR CANVAS at 208, and S and T came out as the
17737               	; 	' scanner's green diagonals on a screen with no radar on it.
17738               	; 	'

17965               	; 	' frames that touched 14 for only four, which made every jump a timing
17966               	; 	' test rather than a decision -- you had to leave the ground on exactly
17967               	; 	' the right frame or clip the thing you were jumping. Widening the
17968               	; 	' plateau rather than raising the apex keeps the ball arithmetic in
17969               	; 	' DESIGN.md 5a intact (the apex is what that depends on) while making the
17970               	; 	' window forgiving: the player still has to CHOOSE to jump, but no longer
17971               	; 	' has to be frame-perfect about it.

18007               	;
18008               	; 	' THE FONT'S COLOUR TABLE WAS 472 BYTES OF ONE REPEATED VALUE, which is a
18009               	; 	' fifth of what the fixed area had left. DEFINE COLOR copies such a table
18010               	; 	' out of ROM into all three screen thirds; writing the constant straight
18011               	; 	' into the colour table does the same job for the price of a loop, and
18012               	; 	' the loop runs once, at boot.
18013               	; 	'
18014               	; 	' The colour table is at >2000 and the VDP mirrors it once per screen
18015               	; 	' third, >800 apart. Both numbers were read out of the GENERATED assembly
18016               	; 	' -- define_color's `ai r0,>2000` and LDIRVM3's `ai r0,>0800` -- rather
18017               	; 	' than assumed, because a wrong base here would paint over the pattern
18018               	; 	' table and the failure would look like corrupt artwork.
18019               	; 	'
18020               	; 	' Paced: a few hundred VDP writes in one frame are silently dropped.
18021               	; 	' THE SCANNER'S COLOURS ARE THREE BLOCKS REPEATED SIXTEEN TIMES EACH, so
18022               	; 	' the table shipped 384 bytes to say 24 bytes' worth. Same trick as the
18023               	; 	' font: write the colour table directly. >2000 is the colour table's base
18024               	; 	' and >800 the stride between screen thirds -- the same layout DEFINE COLOR
18025               	; 	' walks for us in setup_font, which this cannot use because it is cheaper to
18026               	; 	' expand 24 bytes here than to ship 384 in the bank.
18027               	; 	' NOTHING IS UNDER THE GROUND FLOOR, SO NOTHING SHOULD BE GREEN THERE.
18028               	; 	' A floor bar is five pixels of yellow over three of the green air
18029               	; 	' belonging to the floor BELOW it (see SLAB), which is right for three of
18030               	; 	' the four bars and wrong for the last one: below floor 0 there is no
18031               	; 	' floor, only the scanner, and the green read as a strip of shop with
18032               	; 	' nothing in it.
18033               	; 	'
18034               	; 	' NO NEW CHARACTER IS NEEDED, BECAUSE THE COLOUR TABLE HAS THREE COPIES
18035               	; 	' -- one per eight screen rows -- and the bands land such that each bar
18036               	; 	' sits in a different third:
18037               	; 	'
18038               	; 	'     band 0 roof   rows  1-5    bar row  5   third 0
18039               	; 	'     band 1        rows  6-10   bar row 10   third 1
18040               	; 	'     band 2        rows 11-15   bar row 15   third 1
18041               	; 	'     band 3 GROUND rows 16-20   bar row 20   third 2
18042               	; 	'
18043               	; 	' so recolouring SLAB in third 2 alone reaches the ground floor's bar and
18044               	; 	' nothing else. The same third also holds the scanner, but the scanner
18045               	; 	' does not use these characters. This is the same mechanism that once hid
18046               	; 	' a bug for months (CLAUDE.md 3A, the blanked-in-one-third note) used
18047               	; 	' deliberately for once.
18048               	; 	'
18049               	; 	' Only the three bottom lines change, and only their BACKGROUND: SLAB has
18050               	; 	' no ink there and SLABE's brick keeps its grey.
18051               	;
18052               	; 	INCLUDE "font.bas"
18053               	; 	' Keystone Kapers font -- GENERATED by assets/genfont.py. Do not edit; regenerate.
18054               	; 	'
18055               	; 	' Characters 32-90 (59 of them), 8 bytes each = 472 bytes. Williams' cabinet face:
18056               	; 	' heavy, squared, flat terminals, no serifs -- drawn 5x7 inside the 8x8 cell so a
18057               	; 	' blank column at the right and a blank row at the bottom keep it legible.
18058               	; 	'
18059               	; 	' Loaded with DEFINE CHAR 32,59,font_bits. The run must be CONTIGUOUS, so slots
18060               	; 	' with no glyph emit blanks rather than being skipped -- a gap would shift every
18061               	; 	' letter after it.

18183               	;
18184               	; 	' THE COLOUR TABLE, 472 bytes of the same value ($B4 = light yellow ink on dark blue).
18185               	; 	'
18186               	; 	' Loaded with DEFINE COLOR 32,59,font_col, which is ONE synchronous call that
18187               	; 	' writes all three screen thirds (define_color always does the LDIRVM3 triple
18188               	; 	' copy). It replaced a VPOKE loop that wrote this one value 1,416 times paced by
18189               	; 	' 24 WAITs -- the largest scripted delay in the boot, and the reason the title
18190               	; 	' screen used to fill in visibly rather than appearing at once.
18191               	; 	'
18192               	; 	' EIGHT BYTES PER CHARACTER, not one. Supply fewer and DEFINE COLOR reads
18193               	; 	' whatever follows in ROM as colour data, with no error at build or run time.
18194               	;
18195               	; #if NES
18196               	; 	' NES uses nes_fcol; omit this identical 472-byte TMS colour table.
18197               	; #else
18198               	; font_col:
18199               cvb_FONT_COL

19519               	; 	INCLUDE "art.bas"
19520               	; 	' Keystone Kapers art -- GENERATED by assets/genart.py. Do not edit; regenerate.
19521               	; 	'
19522               	; 	' EVERY SPRITE IS 16x16: sprite size and magnification are GLOBAL on the
19523               	; 	' TMS9918, so small objects are drawn small INSIDE a 16x16 box rather than
19524               	; 	' being small sprites.
19525               	; 	'
19526               	; 	' EVERY 8-PX OBJECT SITS IN ROWS 8-15 OF ITS BOX, ducked Kelly included, so
19527               	; 	' one rule places them all: bottom edge = y + 16, and a thing resting on the
19528               	; 	' floor is at y = FLOORY - 16.
19529               	; 	'
19530               	; 	' Sprite bytes are QUADRANT-ORDERED: 16 rows of the left half, then 16 of
19531               	; 	' the right. Every block is an EVEN number of bytes -- an odd DATA BYTE run
19532               	; 	' silently misaligns every word table after it (CLAUDE.md 3A).
19533               	;
19534               	; spr_kelly:	' Kelly: RIGHT hat/face/two merged run bodies/two FREE slots/duck hat/face/body, then the same LEFT (+36). The run bodies carry tunic AND legs, so a frame is one sprite, and standing is run frame 1. Patterns 0..68
19535               cvb_SPR_KELLY

20648               	;
20649               	; 	' -------------------------------------------------- scanner canvas
20650               	; 	' Chars 208-255: 16 cols x 3 rows over screen rows 21-23. Blank to start;
20651               	; 	' dots are plotted by VPOKEing the PATTERN table (rows 21-23 sit in the
20652               	; 	' third screen third, so every scanner pattern is at base 4096).
20653               	;
20654               	; 	' --------------------------------------------------- font colours
20655               	; 	' Chars 32-90, EIGHT bytes each. Without this the font keeps whatever
20656               	; 	' CVBasic left in the colour table, which on a green store made the HUD
20657               	; 	' unreadable.
20658               	;
20659               	; esc_deck:	' 6 x (char, 8 colour bytes) -- write into the THIRD-0 colour table at 8192 + char*8, once, at setup
20660               cvb_ESC_DECK

     7190 1A1A

20766               	; 	INCLUDE "store.bas"
20767               	; 	' Keystone Kapers store -- GENERATED by assets/genstore.py. Do not edit.
20768               	; 	'
20769               	; 	' EIGHT band templates of 5 rows x 32 cols (160 bytes each) plus a 32-byte
20770               	; 	' index over (level, screen). The whole 8-screen, 4-level building is about
20771               	; 	' 1.3 KB instead of the 5,120 bytes it would cost to store literally.
20772               	; 	'
20773               	; 	' All eight templates are ONE contiguous block under ONE label, so a band
20774               	; 	' blit is
20775               	; 	'     SCREEN stor_tpl, tpl*160, toprow*32, 32, 5, 32
20776               	; 	' with no label ladder -- SCREEN needs a literal label and a label cannot be
20777               	; 	' chosen by a variable, which is why RallyX needed a 4-way IF over its maze
20778               	; 	' tables. One block sidesteps it.
20779               	; 	'
20780               	; 	' 160 is EVEN, so this cannot leave the location counter odd and misalign
20781               	; 	' the word tables defined after it.
20782               	; 	'
20783               	; 	' template ids:
20784               	; 	'   0 T_AISLE_A
20785               	; 	'   1 T_AISLE_B
20786               	; 	'   2 T_ESC_W
20787               	; 	'   3 T_ESC_E
20788               	; 	'   4 T_ELEV
20789               	; 	'   5 T_ROOF0
20790               	; 	'   6 T_ROOF1
20791               	; 	'   7 T_ROOF2
20792               	; 	'   8 T_ROOF3
20793               	; 	'   9 T_ROOF4
20794               	; 	'   10 T_ROOF5
20795               	; 	'   11 T_ROOF6
20796               	; 	'   12 T_ROOF7
20797               	; 	'   13 T_END_W
20798               	; 	'   14 T_END_E
20799               	;
20800               	; stor_tpl:	' 15 templates x 160 bytes

21416               	;
21417               	; 	' THE SKYLINE'S LAST BAND WITHOUT ITS YELLOW, high nibble ink, low nibble
21418               	; 	' paper, one byte a scan line -- the same shape genart emits into
21419               	; 	' store_col. SKY2 is white-on-9 throughout instead of turning to paper 10
21420               	; 	' at row 4; BLDGL holds its blue one row longer and then meets its own
21421               	; 	' grey wall. Both are the generated bytes with 10 replaced by 9 and
21422               	; 	' nothing else changed. See setup_rest.
21423               	; #if NES
21424               	; nes_sky2c:
21425               	; 	DATA BYTE $F9,$F9,$F9,$F9,$F9,$F9,$F9,$F9
21426               	; nes_bldlc:
21427               	; 	DATA BYTE $B9,$B9,$B9,$B9,$B9,$BE,$BE,$BE
21428               	; #endif
21429               	;
21430               	; 	' THE IN-GAME FONT'S COLOUR, one byte a scan line and eight a character for
21431               	; 	' all 59 of them. $B4 is light yellow on dark blue -- ink index 3, paper index 1 --
21432               	; 	' and which colours those are is then the attribute table's business, per
21433               	; 	' region: dark blue behind the HUD, the store's green behind a message box.
21434               	; 	'
21435               	; 	' 472 bytes of one repeated value. That reads like waste and is the cheap
21436               	; 	' option: ROM is three budgets here and this is not the scarce one, while
21437               	; 	' the alternative is a second font (impossible -- only eleven free codes)
21438               	; 	' or a new uploader parameter (no RAM -- two bytes left).
